cards.back: let: block-scoped, reassignable. const: block-scoped, not reassignable. var: function-scoped, hoisted, avoid in modern JS.
string, number, bigint, boolean, undefined, null, symbol. Immutable and compared by value.
=== (strict equality): no type coercion. == (loose equality): coerces types before comparing. Always prefer ===.
A function that retains access to its outer scope's variables even after the outer function has returned.
Variable and function declarations are moved to the top of their scope during compilation. var is hoisted (undefined); let/const are hoisted but not initialized (TDZ).

const fn = (a, b) => a + b;
No own 'this' binding — inherits from enclosing scope. Cannot be used as constructors.
Refers to the execution context. In methods: the object. In functions: global (or undefined in strict mode). Arrow functions: lexical 'this'.
Mechanism that executes code, processes events, and runs queued callbacks. Call stack → microtasks (Promises) → macrotasks (setTimeout).
Object representing eventual completion/failure of an async operation. States: pending → fulfilled or rejected. Chain with .then() and .catch().
async function returns a Promise. await pauses execution until the Promise resolves. Syntactic sugar over .then() chains.
Expands iterables: [...arr1, ...arr2], {...obj1, ...obj2}. Useful for shallow copies and merging.
Collects remaining arguments into an array: function fn(a, ...rest) { }. Must be the last parameter.
Backtick strings with embedded expressions: `Hello, ${name}!`. Support multi-line strings and tagged templates.
Creates a new array by applying a function to each element. [1,2,3].map(x => x * 2) → [2,4,6]. Does not mutate.
Creates a new array with elements that pass a test. [1,2,3,4].filter(x => x > 2) → [3,4]. Does not mutate.
Reduces an array to a single value. arr.reduce((acc, cur) => acc + cur, 0). Accumulator starts at initial value.
Executes a function for each element. Returns undefined (not chainable). Use map/filter/reduce for transformations.
find() returns the first matching element (or undefined). findIndex() returns the first matching index (or -1).
keys(): array of property names. values(): array of values. entries(): array of [key, value] pairs.
Safely access nested properties: obj?.a?.b. Returns undefined if any part is null/undefined instead of throwing.

Returns right operand when left is null or undefined (not for 0 or '').
const val = input ?? 'default';

cards.front: What is a Map vs Object?
cards.back: Map: any key type, ordered, size property, iterable. Object: string/symbol keys, prototype chain. Use Map for frequent add/remove.
Collection of unique values. new Set([1,2,2,3]) → {1,2,3}. Methods: add, delete, has, size.
JavaScript Object Notation. Text format for data exchange. JSON.stringify(obj) and JSON.parse(str). Keys must be double-quoted strings.
Document Object Model. Tree representation of HTML. JS can read/modify elements: document.querySelector(), element.textContent, etc.
Attach one event listener to a parent instead of each child. Uses event bubbling. Check event.target to identify the clicked child.
localStorage: persists until cleared. sessionStorage: cleared when tab closes. Both store strings, ~5MB limit, same-origin only.

Modern API for HTTP requests. Returns a Promise.
fetch(url).then(r => r.json()).then(data => ...)
Supports GET, POST, headers, body.
Objects inherit from their prototype (__proto__). Property lookups traverse the chain until found or null. Basis of JS inheritance.

cards.front: What is a class in JS?

cards.back: Unique, immutable primitive. Used for non-string property keys. Symbol('desc') always creates a new symbol. Symbol.for() creates shared symbols.

function* gen() { yield 1; yield 2; }
Returns an iterator. Lazily produces values. Pauses at each yield.

try { risky code } catch (err) { handle error } finally { always runs }.
Errors have message and stack properties.
Unary operator returning a string: 'string', 'number', 'boolean', 'object', 'function', 'undefined', 'symbol', 'bigint'. Note: typeof null === 'object' (historical bug).
Debounce: delay execution until no calls for N ms (search input). Throttle: execute at most once per N ms (scroll handler).
Not changing existing data. Create new objects instead: spread ({...obj, key: val}), Object.freeze() (shallow). Libraries: Immer, Immutable.js.
Like Map/Set but keys (WeakMap) or values (WeakSet) are weakly held — garbage-collected if no other references. Keys must be objects.

condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse
Short form of if/else for expressions. Can be nested but avoid for readability.
